title: The bottle that went green
scenario:
A juice brand approved a 5-second clip: a bottle turns slowly on a sunny counter. Now the client wants an evening version with the new green cap. The bottle, the turn and the framing must stay as approved. Your teammate drafted the edit requests and sent them to you before running anything.

Use the exhibit. The field names and rules are from Luma's and Google's docs (October 2026). The brand, the ids and the plan are made up for this case.
exhibit:
LUMA EDIT DRAFT (made up)
  model:                    ray-3.2
  type:                     video_edit
  source.generation_id:     a1f0... (the approved clip)
  aspect_ratio:             9:16   (for the stories version)
  video.edit.strength:      reimagine_3
  video.edit.auto_controls: true
  video.edit.controls:      depth enabled
  prompt: "A glass juice bottle with a green cap turns on a
           wooden counter in a modern kitchen at dusk. Warm lamps,
           blue window light, plants, a fruit bowl, a tiled wall..."

GOOGLE PLAN (made up)
  Gemini Omni Flash, conversational edit of the same clip.
  Turn 1: the cap. Turn 2: the evening light.

questions.prompt: Luma would refuse the draft as written. Which two settings clash?

options.text: auto_controls set to true with depth controls
options.explanation: Right. The Luma docs say controls cannot be combined with auto_controls: true. Pick one of the two.
A prior Luma generation id is one of the ways Luma takes a source for an edit.

options.text: type video_edit with a prompt for the scene
options.explanation: An edit re-renders the clip under a new prompt. A long prompt is a style problem, not a rule clash.

options.text: strength set with a generation id source
options.explanation: Luma accepts strength on an edit of a prior generation. That pair is fine.

questions.prompt: The bottle and the turn must stay as approved. Which strength fits a relight and a cap change?

options.text: Keep reimagine_3, so the new light looks as strong as it can
options.explanation: In the Reimagine band the prompt drives most of the output. The approved turn and framing could change.

options.text: A value in the Adhere band, which keeps the source motion and framing
options.explanation: Right. Adhere closely preserves source motion, composition and structure. That is what a relight needs (our advice).

options.text: Any value, because strength only changes the price of the edit
options.explanation: Strength is the dial for how much of the source is kept, not a price setting.

options.text: reimagine_1, since it is the lightest step in the strongest band
options.explanation: It is lighter than reimagine_3, but still in the band where the prompt drives most of the output.

questions.prompt: The draft sets aspect_ratio to 9:16 for a stories version. What will happen?

options.text: Luma will crop the clip to 9:16 from the centre
options.explanation: Luma does not crop on an edit. It ignores the setting and keeps the source's shape.

options.text: Luma will outpaint the clip to a 9:16 frame
options.explanation: Outpainting (adding new picture beyond the edges) is a different request type. That is chapter 6, not an edit.

options.text: Luma will ignore it and keep the source shape
options.explanation: Right. The Luma docs say the output preserves the source's aspect ratio, and aspect_ratio on an edit is silently ignored.

options.text: Luma will refuse the request with a 400 error
options.explanation: The Luma docs say the setting is silently ignored, not rejected. That is why it is easy to miss.

questions.prompt: On Gemini Omni Flash, the first edit turn changes only the cap. Which prompt fits the advice in the Gemini API docs?

options.text: "A bottle with a green cap turns on a wooden counter, with lamps and plants."
options.explanation: This describes the whole scene again. The Gemini API docs say overly descriptive prompts can lead to unintended changes.

options.text: "Change the cap to bright green. Keep everything else the same."
options.explanation: Right. The Gemini API docs say simple prompts work best for video editing, and to add Keep everything else the same. The light can be the next turn.

options.text: "Make a brand new video of this juice bottle with a green cap."
options.explanation: That asks for a new video. The client approved the turn and framing of this one.

options.text: "Edit the video. Change whatever you need so the cap looks right."
options.explanation: This names no change and no limits. The model could change the bottle or the motion.
